answer.rationale: Judged strictly on distance from the objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue) and on what each note omits. memory_57 rates highest (4): it is the only entry that names qualified revenue directly AND reports a negative check (no measurable retention harm), i.e. it tests durability rather than just lift; it still omits magnitude, cohort size, and how referral-sourced accounts age past the first period. memory_44 (3) speaks to pipeline quality, a reasonable revenue proxy in enterprise, but pipeline is not booked or retained revenue and the note omits win rates, cycle length, and cost-to-serve of the sales-assisted path. memory_31 (3) is the only note claiming a durable lift, which is meaningful, but the durability is asserted for activation, not revenue, and it omits whether easier signup changed lead quality — fewer required fields can raise activation while diluting the accounts that activate. memory_73 (2) is the most seductive item this week because it maps onto the competitor pricing threat, and it does claim revenue lift — but it omits everything that determines whether that revenue is sustainable: discount depth, margin, renewal and retention of promo-acquired cohorts, and whether the lift was pull-forward. A promotional response to a competitor's entry pricing is exactly the case where short-window revenue lift and long-term qualified revenue can diverge, so the note's silence is disqualifying rather than neutral. memory_86 (2) reports completion and time-to-value, upstream proxies with no revenue or retention linkage. memory_91 is weakest (1): week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action' are the most distal proxies in the set, with no revenue tie, no retention check, no durability window, and no indication the nudged accounts differ in value from unnudged ones. Overall caution: every memory is a consolidated summary with the source archived, so none can be re-audited for effect size, sample, or confounds; all six are single-direction positive findings, which suggests survivorship in what got consolidated. Two of the three current problems (activation -6%, onboarding -4%) sit precisely where memories 31, 86, and 91 claimed durable wins, which is itself evidence that those recorded lifts decayed or were measured too early — a reason to discount them further, not to simply re-run them.
